title: Add auditor and warden roles from the 2026-10-16 addendum
summary: Implement the BRIEF addendum for the owner: an auditor role that judges real outcomes against BRIEF.md and owner goals, and a warden role/check that holds any landing touching protected files or weakening a check. It follows how the audience role was added (role, core module, CLI command, tests, design doc).

defaults_applied.how: New unit and CLI tests; cargo test, clippy and fmt --check pass.
Protection is enforced by code in the landing path, not prose.
A design doc in docs/design/ records alternatives.
Tests exercise holds on protected landings and an ordinary landing that still lands.
The auditor judges real outcomes against BRIEF.md and owner goals.
The docs and CHANGELOG are written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: the owner wants grading kept inside Athena, with a protected yardstick; the owner and verifier are the audience.
The protected list lives in one Rust constant in a new warden module, not in athena.toml, so no governance file changes.
The warden is a mechanical check in the landing path, plus a role definition with a short fixed prompt.
The auditor is invoked via a CLI command, like audience, and runs through the fake agent in tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`: tests pass showing a landing that modifies BRIEF.md, an auditor or warden prompt, a grader prompt or threshold, or a permission, budget or kill-switch setting is held with a recorded reason, while an ordinary landing still lands.
Run `cargo test`: a test shows a landing that deletes a test or lowers a threshold (loosens a check) is held.
Run `cargo test`: a test shows a job's change to the auditor's or warden's prompts or checks is held.
Run `cargo test`: an auditor run through the fake agent records a verdict that cites evidence of a real outcome.
Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`: both clean.

crates/athena-data/src/roles.rs defines valid `auditor` and `warden` RoleDefinitions with short fixed prompts and tests; the auditor prompt says to judge against BRIEF.md and owner goals, not the job's criteria, and to look at real outcomes.
A design doc and a CHANGELOG entry explain both roles, the protected list, the alternatives, and that only the owner changes these rules; the protected list is defined in one place.

out_of_scope: Changing BRIEF.md, athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
Retrofitting the existing grader or verifier roles
Owner-side tooling to edit the protected list
departures: Larger than the reference: a new core module, role definitions, CLI wiring and two test suites, with a landing-path hook.
